<!--
Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines;
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

For additional information on our contributing process, read our contributing
guide https://docs.docker.com/opensource/code/

If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
"closes #xxxx"

Please provide the following information:
-->

**- What I did**

Fixes #41920

- Passing only `a` is now allowed
- When one passes only `a`, a cgroup rule allowing all permissions is returned
- If an `a` type rule is passed but is not `a *:* rwm` (`rwm` can be reordered), an error is returned informing the user that the rest of their rule is ineffective ([reference](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v5.10/Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v1/devices.rst))
- Changed the validation of `major` and `minor` numbers so that they are 12 and 20 bits respectively
- Changed the behavior of all (`*`) major or minor numbers to just omit the field in the cgroup permission, as per the [runtime-spec](https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/blob/v1.0.2/config-linux.md#device-whitelist)
- Updated `oci` tests to reflect these changes
- Moved cgroup validation to container create, instead of container start
- Changed the name of the `AppendDevicePermissionsFromCgroupRules` function to `DevicePermissionsFromCgroupRules` and changed the parameters to reflect that it doesn't need to do any appending anymore
- Added an `errdef` for an error returned by the `DevicePermissionsFromCgroupRules` function and added tests for that `errdef`

One more thing the issue calls for is either updating the CLI or removing the client-side validation. This seems like a decision that has to be made, so I decided to leave it out of this PR for now. I'd be happy to add it once an agreement has been reached.

Also, I just noticed that the regex allows rules such as `c 1:1 rrr` and `b 1:1 wmm`. Should it?

**- How I did it**

- To validate the `a` type rules, I added a function that checks the rule to see if it is either a singular `a` or, for example, a `a 1:5 w`. I then added a second regex that parses the rule to make sure that it's either `a` or `a *:* rwm` (`rwm` can be reordered), and throw an error telling the user that their rule is ineffective if the regex doesn't pass.
- Previously, the cgroup rule validation took place in the `WithDevices` function, which is called through `daemon.createSpec`, which is called on container start. `AppendDevicePermissionsFromCgroupRules` is passed a field from the config (`HostConfig.DeviceCgroupRules`), which is actually set on container create. So, I moved `AppendDevicePermissionsFromCgroupRules` to right after that field is set in container create, and set the result of it to a new field (`HostConfig.DeviceCgroupPermissions`). Because that `WithDevices` function has access to the config, I replaced the block of code that ran the function with one that just appends `HostConfig.DeviceCgroupPermissions` to the accumulated `devPermissions`. A similar pattern exists in `oci_windows.go`, and I did the same there. Because this function is now not appending to any existing value, just being used to set a field, I decided to change the name to `DevicePermissionsFromCgroupRules` and remove the parameter that provided the existing value.

**- How to verify it**

- Run `oci` tests

```shell
curl -v --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock \
"http://localhost/v1.41/containers/create?name=foobar" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"Image":"hello-world", "HostConfig":{"DeviceCgroupRules": ["invalid rule"]}}'
```

`{"message":"invalid device cgroup rule format: 'invalid rule'"}`

**- Description for the changelog**
<!--
Write a short (one line) summary that describes the changes in this
pull request for inclusion in the changelog:
-->

`Improved device cgroup rule parsing and moved it to container create`

issue_context.title: Improve validation and handling of `--device-cgroup-rule`
issue_context.body:
As a follow-up to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/41919

Validation, and handling of `--device-cgroup-rule` could use some improvements.

### 1. Improve handling/validation of "a (all)" value

We currently treat `a` the same as other (`c (char)`, `b (block)`) devices. However, the [kernel documentation](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v5.10/Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v1/devices.rst) describes:

```markdown
... A device cgroup associates a device access whitelist with each cgroup. A whitelist
entry has 4 fields. 'type' is a (all), c (char), or b (block). 'all' means it applies
to all types and all major and minor numbers. Major and minor are either an integer
or * for all. Access is a composition of r (read), w (write), and m (mknod).
```

In addition, that documentation shows an example where _only_ the device-type is passed;

```console
echo a > /sys/fs/cgroup/1/devices.allow
```

Related source code: https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v5.10/security/device_cgroup.c#L614-L642

From the above;

- passing only `a` should is allowed
- passing only `a` is equivalent to "all" device-types, "all" major/minor numbers, and "all" permissions, so equivalent to `a *:* rwm`
- when passing `a` in combination with `major:minor` and `[rwm]` permissions, both major/minor, and permissions are ignored

I think we should:

- consider allowing `a` as valid value
- in that case, either;
    - ignore `major:minor` and `[rwm`, and warn that these fields are ignored (?)
    - produce an error if the fields are not `*:*` and `rwm` respectively (note: permissions can be ordered in any way, so `rwm` and `mwr` are equivalent)

### 2. Improve validation of major/minor

Looks like we currently don't validate against if the major/minor is in the correct range; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v5.10/include/linux/kdev_t.h
(12 bits are used to encode a major number (0..4095, it seems), 20 bits); https://stackoverflow.com/a/14849363

### 3. Validate on container "create" instead of on "start"

Validation doesn't take place until the container is started; we should validate the value when creating the container, so that we can fail early.

### 4. Update CLI accordingly, or remove client-side validation

We shouldn't validate this value on the client side, and just delegate validation to the daemon/API; if we _do_ want to keep client-side validation, the rules should match what the daemon accepts (if we update).
comments: For validating major/minor, we can probably use some of the functionality provided by golang.org/x/sys (e.g. https://github.com/golang/sys/blob/e293359b922457499663dd8350d511d3cca6ac37/unix/dev_linux.go#L21)
Seems that this issue is resolved, could someone prove it, please?
Hi @thaJeztah I would like to know if a proposal for this issue is still needed? I am interested in working on it if it's not assigned to someone already

review_comments:
Existing containers won't have the new `DeviceCgroupPermissions` field, so with this change, will no longer have their `DeviceCgroupRules` applied after upgrading.

We should probably keep the conversion here (as well), but may have to be either "less" strict here (ignore the "previously accepted" format), or have a migration step somewhere during the "restore" step (when starting the daemon); similar to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/22575 (which we'll be removing in https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/41756)

I never thought about that aspect, thanks! I would put forth adding a migration step to avoid adding more logic to the validation function, and because the validation only really needs to happen once. That being said, I can see why having those kinds of things around could be undesirable. Up to you.

w.r.t. Major/Minor `nil` being equivalent to `-1` (runtime-spec); Looks indeed that runc uses these as a default, and only override in the "not nil" situation; https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/blob/ee06c700dcb34504204cb171bb35e0e01477bf58/libcontainer/specconv/spec_linux.go#L475-L487

Should we check if other runtimes (e.g. `crun` handle it the same?)
